newsitem.title: BRAZIL: IMF sees Brazil missing 2.5 pct deficit goal.
newsitem.headline: IMF sees Brazil missing 2.5 pct deficit goal.

text.p: Brazil is unlikely to achieve its aim of a 2.5 percent of Gross Domestic Product operational public sector deficit this year but the result will be better than 1995, an International Monetary Fund director said.
"The fiscal results, although probably not as good as had been hoped at the start of the year, will be better than last year," Lorenzo Perez, the IMF's Western Hemisphere director told reporters.
Perez was attending an International Seminar on Public Finances in Brasilia.
He said the 1996 result may prove to be "a little bit higher" than the government's target of halving last year's operational deficit to 2.5 percent from 5.0 percent of GDP.
But he said it would be better than the 3.5 percent operational deficit notched up in the first half of 1996.
Perez said the first half of the year had been affected by lower economic output than during the same period of 1995. He said better export performance would spur an improvement in the second half.
But he added there was a risk from high spending in the run-up to the October municipal elections.
